chunks.text: import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime"; applySeo({ title: "New Page", description: "..." }); ``` See [SPA Runtime](./spa-runtime.md). The plugin exports types for every config shape: - `SeoPluginOptions` - options accepted by `seo()` - `SeoOptions` - the full beeg config (site, pages, robots, sitemap, validate) - `SiteConfig` - site defaults - `PageMeta` - per-page overrides - `OpenGraphInfo` - Open Graph values - `TwitterInfo` - Twitter Card values - `FaviconConfig` - favicon and platform icons - `RobotsFileOptions` - robots.txt options - `RobotsGroup` - an RFC 9309 agent group - `SitemapOptions` - sitemap options - `ImageRef` / `ImageInput` - image references, including `thumbnail` for video sitemaps - `JsonLdConfig` - JSON-LD configuration - `HreflangAlternate` - a hreflang entry - `ThemeColorEntry` - a theme color meta tag - `TwitterCardType` - `summary` \| `summary_large_image` \| `player` \| `app` - `TwitterHandle` - a Twitter `@handle` - `TwitterAppPlatform` - `iphone` \| `ipad` \| `googleplay` - `TwitterPlayer` - player card iframe config - `TwitterApps` - app card per-platform config - `ArticleJsonLd` / `OrganizationJsonLd` / `WebSiteJsonLd` / `ProductJsonLd` / `JsonLdPerson` - JSON-LD shapes - `OpenGraphArticle` / `OpenGraphBook` / `OpenGraphMusic` / `OpenGraphVideo` / `OpenGraphPayment` - Open Graph verticals - `SitemapChangefreq` - changefreq enum - `RobotsDirectives` - structured robots meta directives

--- title: "Installation" description: "Install vite-plugin-seo-meta and set up its peer dependency." --- Install the plugin (It (obviously) needs Vite as a peer dependency). ```bash npm i -D vite-plugin-seo-meta vite ``` Vite 5 or newer is required. The plugin is ESM only. If your project is CommonJS, switch to ESM (easier said than done, to be fair) or use the `.cjs` build.

chunks.heading: Build output
chunks.text: ``` Vite 5 or newer is required. The plugin is ESM only. If your project is CommonJS, switch to ESM (easier said than done, to be fair) or use the `.cjs` build. The plugin builds to `dist/index.js` (ESM) and `dist/index.cjs` (CommonJS). The runtime helper is a separate entry (as why would you want to compile a vite-plugin for web, and vice versa): ```ts import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime"; ``` Importing the runtime pulls in the client-side navigation handler. It is tree-shaken (aka, yeeted) out of the main build if you do not use it.

--- title: "Quick Start" description: "Add SEO to a Vite app in two minutes." --- Add the plugin to `vite.config.ts` and give it a `site` block. Nicely enough, that's the minimum effort you have to do, as everything else gets sensible defaults. Please _do_ fill out the rest though haha, it's worth it. ```ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; import { seo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ seo({ site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site", title: "My Site", titleTemplate: "%s | My Site", description: "My awesome site", }, }), ], }); ```

chunks.heading: Per-page overrides
chunks.text: from "vite-plugin-seo-meta"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ seo({ site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site", title: "My Site", titleTemplate: "%s | My Site", description: "My awesome site", }, }), ], }); ``` Put a `seo.config.ts` next to `vite.config.ts` and the plugin loads it automatically, no questions asked. ```ts import { defineSeoConfig } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta"; export default defineSeoConfig({ site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site", title: "My Site", titleTemplate: "%s | My Site", description: "My awesome site", }, pages: { "/about": { title: "About Us", description: "Who we are and what we build.", }, "/blog/hello-world": { title: "Hello, world", description: "My first post on this site.", noindex: true, }, }, }); ```

chunks.heading: How the puzzle assembles
chunks.text: "/about": { title: "About Us", description: "Who we are and what we build.", }, "/blog/hello-world": { title: "Hello, world", description: "My first post on this site.", noindex: true, }, }, }); ``` - `site` holds the defaults every page inherits - `pages` overrides specific routes. A page can set any field the site has, plus `noindex`, `canonical`, `alternates` and `robots` - The plugin merges site defaults with the matching page, then outputs tags at build time

--- title: "hreflang" description: "Tell search engines which language and region variant of a page to show." --- hreflang alternates are emitted as `<link rel="alternate">` tags. They live in `pages[].alternates`. ```ts pages: { "/": { alternates: [ { hreflang: "en", href: "https://example.com/" }, { hreflang: "es", href: "https://example.com/es/" }, { hreflang: "x-default", href: "https://example.com/" }, ], }, } ``` ![alt text](./assets/images/hreflang.png)

chunks.heading: What each field means
chunks.text: `pages[].alternates`. ```ts pages: { "/": { alternates: [ { hreflang: "en", href: "https://example.com/" }, { hreflang: "es", href: "https://example.com/es/" }, { hreflang: "x-default", href: "https://example.com/" }, ], }, } ``` ![alt text](./assets/images/hreflang.png) - `hreflang`: the language or region code. Use [ISO 639-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639-1_codes) for languages, or `en-US`, `es-MX` for language-region pairs. Region codes come from [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2) which are the two-letter country codes - `href`: the **absolute** URL of that variant - `x-default`: a catch-all for searchers who do not match any listed language or region. Point it at your default page

chunks.heading: Rules
chunks.text: two-letter country codes - `href`: the **absolute** URL of that variant - `x-default`: a catch-all for searchers who do not match any listed language or region. Point it at your default page - Every `href` must be an absolute URL - The page should list itself in its own alternates. If the page is the English variant, include `{ hreflang: "en", href: "https://example.com/" }` - The plugin emits `xhtml:link` alternates in `sitemap.xml` for pages that have hreflang companions - hreflang URLs must all resolve to the same host. The sitemap enforces this.

So, obviously, don't mess up your deployments.

--- title: "JSON-LD" description: "Structured data for search engines: Organization, WebSite, Article, Product, BreadcrumbList and ImageObject." --- JSON-LD, also known as JSON Linked Data, is a way to provide structured data to search engines. It is a standard format for describing the content of a web page for better indexing and results.This plugin emits JSON-LD as `<script type="application/ld+json">` blocks. Enable the types you need in `site.jsonLd` and add per-page data in `pages[].jsonLd`. ![example JSON-LD](./assets/images/json-ld.png) The format is pretty well standardized at [json-ld.org](https://json-ld.org/) and the vocabulary for what you can describe lives at [schema.org](https://schema.org/). The plugin models the common types from schema.org; anything not covered goes through `extra`! If you feel that any type is missing or should be added to the plugin, please open an issue or PR, I'd love to add it!

--- title: "Meta Tags" description: "How the plugin emits title, description, canonical and robots meta tags." --- The plugin emits standard meta tags (`<meta>` tags) for every page. You set the defaults in `site` and override per page in `pages`.

chunks.heading: title
chunks.text: emits title, description, canonical and robots meta tags." --- The plugin emits standard meta tags (`<meta>` tags) for every page. You set the defaults in `site` and override per page in `pages`. The `<title>` comes from the page `title`, falling back to `site.title`. The `titleTemplate` wraps it. You can pass a string or a function to `titleTemplate`. The string should contain `%s` where the page title should go. The function receives the page title and returns a string, for example: ```ts site: { title: "My Site", titleTemplate: "%s | My Site", }, pages: { "/about": { title: "About Us" } }, ``` Renders as `<title>About Us | My Site</title>`. Keep titles under 60 characters. The validator enforces this, and it's generally a good idea to follow it: titles that are too long may be truncated in search results... and that's bad.

chunks.heading: description
chunks.text: Keep titles under 60 characters. The validator enforces this, and it's generally a good idea to follow it: titles that are too long may be truncated in search results... and that's bad. The `<meta name="description">` comes from the page `description`, falling back to `site.description`. ```ts site: { description: "My awesome site" }, pages: { "/about": { description: "Who we are and what we build." } }, ``` Keep descriptions between 50 and 160 characters. Also enforced.

chunks.heading: canonical
chunks.text: ```ts site: { description: "My awesome site" }, pages: { "/about": { description: "Who we are and what we build." } }, ``` Keep descriptions between 50 and 160 characters. Also enforced. `<link rel="canonical">` points to the page URL. It defaults to `site.url + route`. Set it explicitly when the same content lives at multiple URLs. ```ts pages: { "/product": { canonical: "https://example.com/products/widget" }, } ``` Canonicals must be absolute URLs. The validator checks this. Google's guidance on canonicals is [available here](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) and it's worth reading if you're ever unsure whether to set one!

chunks.heading: robots meta
chunks.text: "https://example.com/products/widget" }, } ``` Canonicals must be absolute URLs. The validator checks this. Google's guidance on canonicals is [available here](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) and it's worth reading if you're ever unsure whether to set one! **Per-page** `robots` adds a `<meta name="robots">` value. It does not touch `robots.txt`, which is generated separately. The valid directives are documented in Google's [robots meta tag reference](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag). The plugin accepts all of them! ```ts pages: { "/private": { robots: "noindex, nofollow" } } ``` `noindex: true` is shorthand for `robots: "noindex"`. It also (obviously)excludes the page from `sitemap.xml`.

chunks.heading: noindex and crawling
chunks.text: reference](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag). The plugin accepts all of them! ```ts pages: { "/private": { robots: "noindex, nofollow" } } ``` `noindex: true` is shorthand for `robots: "noindex"`. It also (obviously)excludes the page from `sitemap.xml`. A page with `noindex: true` tells crawlers not to index it, but by default it does not add a `Disallow` rule to `robots.txt`. Crawlers can still reach the page to see the `noindex` directive. This is done because some crawlers (like Googlebot) still index pages... even if they're marked `noindex`, cause Google just do be like that sometimes. To block crawling outright, set `disallowNoindex: true` on the `robots` config: ```ts robots: { disallowNoindex: true; } ```

chunks.heading: Favicon and platform icons (subject to change)
chunks.text: pages... even if they're marked `noindex`, cause Google just do be like that sometimes. To block crawling outright, set `disallowNoindex: true` on the `robots` config: ```ts robots: { disallowNoindex: true; } ``` The `favicon` block emits link tags and meta tags for browsers and platforms: ```ts site: { favicon: { icon: "/favicon.ico", appleTouchIcon: "/apple-touch-icon.png", appleTouchIconPrecomposed: "/apple-touch-icon-precomposed.png", manifest: "/manifest.json", maskIcon: "/mask-icon.svg", maskIconColor: "#000000", mobileWebApp: { title: "My App", capable: true, statusBarStyle: "black-translucent", }, msapplication: { tileColor: "#ffffff", tileImage: "/tile.png", config: "/browserconfig.xml", }, }, } ``` - `maskIconColor` defaults to `#000000` - `mobileWebApp` covers `apple-mobile-web-app-title`, `apple-mobile-web-app-capable` and `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style` - `msapplication` covers `msapplication-TileColor`, `msapplication-TileImage` and `msapplication-config` I plan to eventually fold this into the main seo block and automatically fill in the various fields and manifest and browserconfig files from the existing data, and also generate all icons from a single source image. For now, you have to provide all of these manually.

--- title: "Open Graph" description: "og:* tags for Facebook, LinkedIn and every platform that reads them." --- Open Graph, also known as `og:*` tags, is a universal standard for describing _how_ a page looks when shared on social media. It's used by Facebook, LinkedIn, Discord, Slack (oh hi Hack Club), and **many** other platforms. Suffice to say, they're important. The spec exists at [ogp.me](https://ogp.me/). > Side note: In my opinion, that's how spec pages should be in my opinion, as it's pretty easy to parse, not 20 pages and written in legalese lol. They are emitted from the `openGraph` block, which inherits from `site` defaults.

chunks.heading: Basic tags
chunks.text: pages should be in my opinion, as it's pretty easy to parse, not 20 pages and written in legalese lol. They are emitted from the `openGraph` block, which inherits from `site` defaults. ```ts pages: { "/": { openGraph: { title: "My Site", description: "My awesome site", type: "website", url: "https://example.com", image: "https://example.com/og.png", siteName: "My Site", locale: "en_US", }, }, } ``` - `type` defaults to `website`. Set `article` for blog posts, `book`, `profile`, `music.*`, `video.*` or others... based on what your page is about. - `url` defaults to the page canonical - `image` defaults to `site.image`

--- title: "robots.txt" description: "Generate robots.txt following RFC 9309 with agent groups, wildcards and crawl delays." --- [RFC 9309](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309.html) defines the robots.txt standard. Originally made by Martijn Koster in 1994 [(the original spec)](https://www.robotstxt.org/orig.html), because robots kept crawling sites and causing a ruckus. (Seems mighty familiar to today's AI bots, doesn't it?) The standard has been (barely) updated over the years, and this plugin implements the latest version. ![image of RFC 9309](./assets/images/Tracer_mvn05nlb.png) It's generated at build time. It can be disabled, replaced, or merged with an existing file.

chunks.heading: Basic rules
chunks.text: (barely) updated over the years, and this plugin implements the latest version. ![image of RFC 9309](./assets/images/Tracer_mvn05nlb.png) It's generated at build time. It can be disabled, replaced, or merged with an existing file. ```ts robots: { userAgent: "*", disallow: ["/api", "*.gif$"], allow: ["/public"], crawlDelay: 5, cleanParam: ["sessionid"], host: "example.com", sitemap: "https://example.com/sitemap.xml", disallowNoindex: true, } ``` - `userAgent`: who the rules apply to. Default `*` - `disallow`: paths to block. Supports `*` (match anything) and `$` (end of string) - `allow`: paths to explicitly permit, overriding `disallow` - `crawlDelay`: delay in seconds - `cleanParam`: URL parameters to ignore when crawling - `host`: the `Host:` record - `sitemap`: URL to advertise, or `false` to omit. Defaults to `site.url + /sitemap.xml` - `disallowNoindex`: also block pages with `noindex: true`

chunks.heading: Wildcards
chunks.text: parameters to ignore when crawling - `host`: the `Host:` record - `sitemap`: URL to advertise, or `false` to omit. Defaults to `site.url + /sitemap.xml` - `disallowNoindex`: also block pages with `noindex: true` `*` matches any sequence of characters. `$` matches the end of the URL. ```ts disallow: ["/api", "*.gif$", "/private/*"]; ``` - `/api` blocks `/api`, `/api/foo`, `/api/foo/bar` (basically anything under it) - `*.gif$` blocks `/img/cat.gif` but not `/img/cat.png` (which... is obviously not a GIF) - `/private/*` blocks everything under `/private` (also `/private/foo`, `/private/foo/bar`, etc.) but not `/private` itself. Use `/private` to block that too. `allow` takes priority when a path matches both. So `allow: ["/public"]` lets crawlers through even if `disallow: ["/"]`.

chunks.heading: Agent groups
chunks.text: (also `/private/foo`, `/private/foo/bar`, etc.) but not `/private` itself. Use `/private` to block that too. `allow` takes priority when a path matches both. So `allow: ["/public"]` lets crawlers through even if `disallow: ["/"]`. Different crawlers get different rules: ```ts robots: { groups: [ { userAgent: "GoogleBot", disallow: ["/private"], crawlDelay: 2, }, { userAgent: "BingBot", allow: ["/"], }, ], } ``` Each group has its own `userAgent`, `disallow`, `allow`, `crawlDelay` and `cleanParam`. The default group (top-level fields) applies to `*`.

chunks.heading: Merge with an existing file
chunks.text: ["/private"], crawlDelay: 2, }, { userAgent: "BingBot", allow: ["/"], }, ], } ``` Each group has its own `userAgent`, `disallow`, `allow`, `crawlDelay` and `cleanParam`. The default group (top-level fields) applies to `*`. By default the plugin preserves `robots.txt` in the output directory and appends generated rules. Duplicates are dropped. To overwrite instead, set `merge: false`: ```ts robots: { merge: false; } ```

chunks.heading: noindex and crawling
chunks.text: to `*`. By default the plugin preserves `robots.txt` in the output directory and appends generated rules. Duplicates are dropped. To overwrite instead, set `merge: false`: ```ts robots: { merge: false; } ``` A page with `noindex: true` tells crawlers not to index it. By default it does not add a `Disallow` rule, so crawlers can still reach the page to see the directive. To block crawling outright: ```ts robots: { disallowNoindex: true; } ```

To block crawling outright: ```ts robots: { disallowNoindex: true; } ``` Append literal lines after the generated rules: ```ts robots: { rules: [ "User-agent: *", "Disallow: /", ], } ``` Use this when the plugin does not cover something. The lines are emitted verbatim.

--- title: "sitemap.xml" description: "Generate sitemap.xml with image, video and news namespaces, plus URL caps." --- A sitemap is an XML file that lists all the pages on your site. It's extremely useful for search engines, as it's a easily parsible list of all your pages. It can also include images, videos and news articles. The protocol is documented at [sitemaps.org](https://www.sitemaps.org/protocol.html). I tried to follow this as closely as possible, but if you notice any discrepancies, please open an issue or PR!!! ![alt text](./assets/images/Tracer_mvmzfk8e.png) `sitemap.xml` is generated at build time from the `pages` map. It lists every route that is not `noindex` and not in `exclude`.

chunks.text: any discrepancies, please open an issue or PR!!! ![alt text](./assets/images/Tracer_mvmzfk8e.png) `sitemap.xml` is generated at build time from the `pages` map. It lists every route that is not `noindex` and not in `exclude`. ```ts sitemap: { exclude: ["/admin", "/login"], maxUrls: 100_000, defaultChangefreq: "weekly", defaultPriority: 0.8, siteUrl: "https://example.com", } ``` - `exclude`: routes to leave out - `maxUrls`: URLs per sitemap file. Default `50000` - `defaultChangefreq`: fallback for pages without one - `defaultPriority`: fallback for pages without one - `siteUrl`: origin used to enforce a single-host sitemap

--- title: "SPA Runtime" description: "Update SEO tags when the URL changes in a single-page app." --- SPA apps have a problem. If you navigate to a new route, the `<title>` and `<meta>` tags do not update. This is because the plugin only injects them at build time.So, the plugin injects tags at build time for the initial HTML. When the client navigates to a new route, the tags do not update on their own so you need to call `applySeo()`. ```ts import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime"; function onRouteChange() { applySeo({ title: "New Page", description: "..." }); } ```

chunks.heading: How it works
chunks.text: tags do not update on their own so you need to call `applySeo()`. ```ts import { applySeo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta/runtime"; function onRouteChange() { applySeo({ title: "New Page", description: "..." }); } ``` `applySeo(page, site?)` merges the page data with the injected site config. Pass `site` explicitly when you need a different site than the one the plugin injected. Omit it and the plugin uses the config from the build. It only updates head elements the plugin manages and your own tags are left alone once the page is loaded!

chunks.heading: What it updates
chunks.text: injected. Omit it and the plugin uses the config from the build. It only updates head elements the plugin manages and your own tags are left alone once the page is loaded! - `<title>` - `<meta name="description">` - `<meta name="robots">` - `<link rel="canonical">` - Open Graph tags - Twitter Card tags - JSON-LD scripts

chunks.heading: When to call it
chunks.text: own tags are left alone once the page is loaded! - `<title>` - `<meta name="description">` - `<meta name="robots">` - `<link rel="canonical">` - Open Graph tags - Twitter Card tags - JSON-LD scripts Call it after every route change. In a router, that is the navigation callback: ```ts // vue-router router.afterEach((to) => { applySeo({ title: to.meta.title, description: to.meta.description }); }); // react-router useEffect(() => { applySeo({ title: location.pathname, description: "..." }); }, [location]); ```

chunks.heading: What it does not do
chunks.text: that is the navigation callback: ```ts // vue-router router.afterEach((to) => { applySeo({ title: to.meta.title, description: to.meta.description }); }); // react-router useEffect(() => { applySeo({ title: location.pathname, description: "..." }); }, [location]); ``` `applySeo` updates tags. It does not push history, change the URL, or update the browser title bar. Your router handles that! Don't just rely on `applySeo` if you're making an SPA (if that wasn't obvious already)! It also does not fetch data, as you should already have it available. Pass the metadata you already have!

chunks.heading: vite-plugin-seo-meta
chunks.text: title: "vite-plugin-seo-meta" description: "All-in-one Vite plugin that generates meta tags, canonical, Open Graph, Twitter Cards, JSON-LD, hreflang, robots.txt and sitemap.xml for your app." --- ::: hero layout:split glow:true <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD025 --> Serverless SEO for Vite. One plugin generates `<title>`, meta tags, canonical URLs, Open Graph, Twitter Cards, JSON-LD, hreflang, `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml`. Zero-config defaults, per-page overrides. Works for SPA, MPA, SSG and prerendered builds. ::: tag "Vite" ::: tag "SEO" ::: tag "TypeScript" ::: button "Quick Start" ./getting-started/quickstart.md icon:play <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD034 --> ::: button "Live Demo" external:https://nellowtcs.me/vite-plugin-seo-meta/demo/ icon:monitor <!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line MD034 --> ::: button "GitHub" external:https://github.com/NellowTCS/vite-plugin-seo-meta icon:github == side ```ts // vite.config.ts import { defineConfig } from "vite"; import { seo } from "vite-plugin-seo-meta"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ seo({ site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site", title: "My Site", titleTemplate: "%s | My Site", description: "My awesome site", }, }), ], }); ``` ::: /hero

chunks.heading: Why this plugin
chunks.text: export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ seo({ site: { url: "https://example.com", name: "My Site", title: "My Site", titleTemplate: "%s | My Site", description: "My awesome site", }, }), ], }); ``` ::: /hero Writing SEO by hand means repeating the same tags for every page, keeping them in sync when the site changes, and forgetting a field on the one page you forget at 3 AM, or deleting mysterious ones that keep your site up top on Google. So... this plugin generates them from a single config and per-page overrides, so the tags are always consistent. It also handles the files that are trés important: - `robots.txt` follows [RFC 9309](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309) and happens to support agent groups, `Allow`/`Disallow` wildcards and `Crawl-delay` - `sitemap.xml` supports image, video and news namespaces with single-host enforcement and a URL capacity (extensible) - Twitter Cards have the typical summary, player and app cards with `:site:id` and `:creator:id` variants - Favicon and platform icons cover `apple-touch-icon`, `mask-icon`, mobile web app and `msapplication` tags

chunks.heading: What it does not do
chunks.text: capacity (extensible) - Twitter Cards have the typical summary, player and app cards with `:site:id` and `:creator:id` variants - Favicon and platform icons cover `apple-touch-icon`, `mask-icon`, mobile web app and `msapplication` tags This plugin does not generate social images or app icons (very **big** _Yet_). That is a future thing I plan to add hehe.
